title: [review] project-LICHEN-worker6-tkjl: removed SHA-256 packet verification in shared vector test
description:
## Location

`rust/lichen-schc/tests/fragmentation_vectors.rs:153-156`

## Problem

The commit removed the `assert_eq!` that compared the SHA-256 digest of expanded test-vector packets against the expected `packet_sha256` field. The replacement code:

```rust
if let Some(packet) = &vector.packet {
    let _data = expand(packet);
    let _expected = vector.packet_sha256.as_ref().unwrap();
}
```

still calls `unwrap()` (panics if sha256 field is missing) and expands the packet, but **never verifies** that the computed hash matches the expected value. This means corrupted or wrong test-vector `packet` values will not be detected, removing a data integrity guard.

The `expand(packet)` result is also dead compute — the hex-decoded bytes are discarded.

## Expected

Either restore the SHA-256 comparison (`assert_eq!(&sha2::Sha256::digest(expand(packet))[..], decode_hex(...))`) or if the `packet_sha256` field is no longer the source of truth for format v2, remove the dead code entirely rather than retaining a no-op block.

## Severity

The test vectors at `test/vectors/schc_fragmentation.json` format v2 still carry `packet_sha256` fields. Without verification, altered or corrupted vector packets would pass this test silently.
